reason: Most pylint-only reports are pylint false positives: in implicit namespace packages (directories without __init__.py, e.g. litellm/llms/xai/, litellm/types/, jaraco/) pylint misnames the module and, when it cannot locate the imported submodule, falls back to the package itself, so `from .handler import XAIRealtime`, `from openai import Omit` (in litellm/types/llms/openai.py) or `import functools` (in jaraco/functools/__init__.py) are reported as self-imports (~70); secondary, a possible BUG: ruff misses genuine `from <current module> import name` (13: gunicorn app/wsgiapp.py, psutil tests, rich live.py), including its own docs example.
evidence: repro this_file.py containing `from this_file import foo` -> pylint W0406, ruff silent (#18972 lists this example as not triggering, attributing it to the file name); import_self.rs `import_from_self` only matches `from <parent> import <self-name>`; a clean pkg/__init__.py with `from .mod import X` -> pylint silent; litellm v1.105.0 has no litellm/llms/xai/__init__.py or litellm/types/__init__.py.

reason: Ruff reports any static value (constant-like and not bound by the comprehension: names, tuples of constants, arithmetic such as `1.0 / 2`), as its docs say, while flake8-comprehensions only reports an ast.Constant value.
evidence: `ruff rule C420`: "It's unnecessary to use a dict comprehension to build a dictionary from an iterable when the value is static"; unnecessary_dict_comprehension_for_iterable.rs: "Don't suggest `dict.fromkeys` if the value is not a constant or constant-like"; flake8_comprehensions requires `isinstance(node.value, ast.Constant)`.

reason: Ruff deliberately also checks the call form (`self.assertRaises(Exception, f, ...)`, `pytest.raises(Exception, f)`, aliases such as scipy's `assert_raises`), as its docs example shows, while bugbear only checks `with` items.
evidence: PR #19063 "Support non-context-manager calls in B017" (merged 2025-07-08, fixes #19050); `ruff rule B017` example: `self.assertRaises(Exception, foo)`; bugbear.py check_for_b017 takes an ast.With node.

reason: Harness artefact: 39 of the 66 ruff-only reports are in files whose flake8 output was lost (see N806); secondary, a possible BUG: ruff strips only leading underscores before the CapWords test, so class names with a trailing underscore (paramiko `Password_`, sqlalchemy `True_`/`False_`, sympy `RuntimeError_`, ~25) are reported, while pep8-naming strips both ends (PEP 8's single_trailing_underscore_ convention); 1 is a `# noqa:  A001` comment (two spaces) that flake8 treats as a blanket noqa.

evidence: `ruff rule B006`: "Arguments with immutable type annotations will be ignored by this rule."

reason: Ruff deliberately also checks `os.environ.get(key, default)` (all 49 ruff-only), and it only judges defaults whose type it can resolve syntactically, while pylint infers named constants (`os.getenv("GCS_BATCH_SIZE", GCS_DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE)`, the 13 pylint-only); the rule docs still mention only os.getenv.

reason: Ruff's rule is documented to check only explicit `raise StopIteration`; pylint's stop-iteration-return also reports `next(it)` calls without a default inside generators, which are all 59 pylint-only reports.

reason: flake8-simplify registers SIM112 on expression statements only, so it never checks `os.environ[...]` or `os.environ.get(...)` inside assignments, conditions or calls (all 55 ruff-only); ruff checks every use.
evidence: flake8_simplify rules/ast_expr.py: `@rule("SIM112", ast.Expr)`; repro `x = os.environ["foo"]` -> ruff SIM112, flake8-simplify silent; a bare statement `os.environ["foo"]` -> both report.

reason: pep8-naming judges a dotted import by its whole path, so `import IPython.testing.tools as tt` or `import fontTools.feaLib.ast as ast` is reported as camelcase imported as lowercase although the imported module is lowercase (24 flake8-only); ruff checks the last component; secondary, a possible BUG: ruff's camelcase test rejects any underscore, so it misses `_WebSocketConnect as connect` (12); 11 ruff-only are markdown files skipped by flake8 (`# flake8: noqa: E501 ...`, CFG).
evidence: pep8ext_naming.py ImportAsCheck uses `name.name` (the full dotted path); ruff pep8_naming/helpers.rs: `is_camelcase(name)` = `!is_cased_lowercase && !is_cased_uppercase && !name.contains('_')`.

reason: Default option: ruff's lint.flake8-import-conventions.aliases contains "xml.etree.ElementTree": "ET" and N817 allows conventional aliases, which covers 50 of the 51 flake8-only reports (`import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET`); the last is `_CustomTextWrap as CTW` (leading underscore, see N813).

reason: pylint deliberately skips a lambda when a name in the called expression is rebound or deleted later (late binding, e.g. `raises(E, lambda: m.f())` followed by `m = ...` in sympy tests); ruff does not, so it reports lambdas whose inlining could change behaviour; an open issue covers the closely related forward-binding case; the pylint-only lines mostly carry `# noqa` (CFG).
evidence: pylint basic_checker.py visit_lambda: `utils.is_reassigned_after_current(node, name.name)`; repro: two lambdas on `m` with `m` reassigned in between -> pylint reports only the second, ruff both; #24704 (open) "PLW0108 false positive if callable is defined later", fix PR #29267 ("any referenced binding ... after the lambda") closed unmerged.

reason: Ruff's rule only checks reassignment of parameters named `self` and `cls`, as documented, while pylint checks the first parameter whatever its name (sympy's `f`, `A`, `K0`, wrapt's `args`).
evidence: `ruff rule PLW0642`: "Checks for assignment of `self` and `cls` in instance and class methods respectively."

reason: Ruff deliberately reports only chains whose returned values are free of side effects and that start at the `if` itself; flake8-simplify also suggests a dict lookup when the branch values are computations or calls (`D - C * inv * B`, `"%s" % name`), which would evaluate every branch eagerly (REF for those).
evidence: if_else_block_instead_of_dict_lookup.rs: "Each if or elif statement's test must consist of a constant equality check with the same variable" and `contains_effect(value, ...)` checks on each returned value.

reason: Ruff's nan-comparison looks at the operands of every comparison regardless of the operator, so it reports membership tests (`np.nan in obj`, 16) and ordering comparisons (12), which pylint limits to ==, !=, is, is not; for `in` the advice to use isnan is wrong, since membership checks identity first (`np.nan in [np.nan]` is True), and ruff's own fixture tests only `==`.
evidence: repro `a = np.nan in obj; b = x < np.nan; c = x == np.nan` -> ruff 3 reports, pylint only the `==`; nan_comparison.rs is called with `compare.operands` only; pylint comparison_checker.py calls _check_nan_comparison only for `==, !=, is, is not`; no issue found.

reason: Documented limitation: ruff only detects built-in exception classes, while pylint also flags user-defined ones (MyExceptionGroup, PydanticKnownError, numpy's AxisError, marshmallow's ValidationError).
evidence: `ruff rule PLW0133` Known problems: "This rule only detects built-in exceptions, like `ValueError`, and does not catch user-defined exceptions."

reason: Ruff reports any truthy literal in an `or` (`1 or g_use_extra`, `7 or ...`), as documented, and replaces the expression with True only in boolean contexts; flake8-simplify suggests `True` for any `... or True`, even in value contexts and when that drops a call (`self.watching and await self.execute_command("UNWATCH") or True`) (REF for the 8 flake8-only).
evidence: `ruff rule SIM222`: "Checks for `or` expressions that contain truthy values... In other cases, the expression can be short-circuited to the first truthy value."
